es: Reconocer formas reducidas frecuentes (gonna, wanna, gotta, dunno, whaddya, lemme, I'd've) en audio rápido, emparejarlas con su forma completa y valorar qué registro transmiten.

teaching.en: I'm gonna call you as soon as the meeting ends, but if it runs late I'll send a message instead.
teaching.es: Te voy a llamar en cuanto termine la reunión, pero si se alarga te mandaré un mensaje en su lugar.
teaching.explanationEs: Gonna es la forma rápida de going to: plan o intención.
segments: I'm gonna call you as soon as the meeting ends,
but if it runs late I'll send a message instead.
teaching.audioText: I'm gonna call you as soon as the meeting ends, but if it runs late I'll send a message instead.

teaching.en: Do you wanna come along to the talk on Friday, or are you kinda tired of conferences by now?
teaching.es: ¿Quieres venir a la charla del viernes, o ya estás un poco harto de las conferencias?
teaching.explanationEs: Wanna es want to; kinda es kind of y suaviza la idea (un poco).
segments: Do you wanna come along to the talk on Friday,
or are you kinda tired of conferences by now?
teaching.audioText: Do you wanna come along to the talk on Friday, or are you kinda tired of conferences by now?

teaching.en: I gotta leave soon, so lemme know whether the plan has changed before I head out.
teaching.es: Tengo que irme pronto, así que avísame si el plan ha cambiado antes de que salga.
teaching.explanationEs: Gotta es have got to (obligación); lemme es let me y se oye en peticiones y ofrecimientos.
segments: I gotta leave soon, so lemme know whether
the plan has changed before I head out.
teaching.audioText: I gotta leave soon, so lemme know whether the plan has changed before I head out.

teaching.en: Honestly, I dunno what he said, because he tends to mumble and slur his words when he's in a hurry.
teaching.es: La verdad es que no sé qué dijo, porque suele hablar entre dientes y arrastrar las palabras cuando tiene prisa.
teaching.explanationEs: Dunno es I don't know; mumble y slur describen a quien se come o arrastra las palabras.
segments: Honestly, I dunno what he said, because he tends to
mumble and slur his words when he's in a hurry.
teaching.audioText: Honestly, I dunno what he said, because he tends to mumble and slur his words when he's in a hurry.

teaching.en: I'd've replied much sooner if I'd seen your text, but my phone was on silent and I dunno how I missed it.
teaching.es: Te habría respondido mucho antes si hubiera visto tu mensaje, pero mi teléfono estaba en silencio y no sé cómo se me pasó.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd've es I would have: expresa algo que no ocurrió. Solo se usa al hablar.
segments: I'd've replied much sooner if I'd seen your text, but my
phone was on silent and I dunno how I missed it.
teaching.audioText: I'd've replied much sooner if I'd seen your text, but my phone was on silent and I dunno how I missed it.

teaching.en: Whaddya think of this transcript? Written down, all those reduced forms can come across as careless in a formal email.
teaching.es: ¿Qué te parece esta transcripción? Por escrito, todas esas formas reducidas pueden dar la impresión de descuido en un correo formal.
teaching.explanationEs: Whaddya es what do you; come across as describe la impresión que causa un texto o un hablante.
segments: Whaddya think of this transcript? Written down, all those reduced
forms can come across as careless in a formal email.
teaching.audioText: Whaddya think of this transcript? Written down, all those reduced forms can come across as careless in a formal email.

prompt.es: Elige la versión completa y fiel del mensaje de voz de Leo.

choices.text: I am going to be late; I want to finish the report first, and I do not know if the client will wait.
I am going to be late; I have got to finish the report first, and I do not know if the client will wait.
I was going to be late; I had got to finish the report first, and I did not know if the client would wait.

feedback.es: Gotta es have got to y expresa obligación, no deseo; gonna y dunno siguen en presente.

hint.es: Gotta marca obligación, no deseo, y el mensaje está en presente.

origin.text: Leo's voice note: 'I'm gonna be late. I gotta finish the report first, and I dunno if the client will wait.'

prompt.es: Completa: estaba agotado y «arrastraba las palabras» al final de la llamada.

feedback.es: Slur your words es la colocación para hablar arrastrando o pegando las palabras, sobre todo por cansancio.

hint.es: Es el verbo que acompaña a «his words» cuando alguien habla mal por el cansancio.

origin.text: He wasn't angry, only exhausted: he didn't shout, he just mumbled and ___ his words at the end of the call.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame revisar la transcripción antes de responder.»

answer.text: Lemme check the transcript before I reply

feedback.es: Lemme sustituye a let me y va seguido del verbo base: lemme check.

hint.es: Empieza por la forma reducida de let me.

prompt.es: Escucha la nota y elige qué le pide la compañera de casa a la narradora.

choices.text: To call her back as soon as she hears the note.
To cover a colleague's shift for her tonight.
Not to stay awake until she gets home.

feedback.es: «Don't wait up» pide no esperarla despierta; quien cubre el turno es la compañera, no la narradora.

origin.audio: My flatmate left a voice note this morning. She said she's gonna be home late because she's gotta cover a colleague's shift, and then she added, I dunno when I'll be back, so don't wait up. She sounded kinda stressed, but she was only in a hurry.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con formas reducidas con su traducción natural.

feedback.es: Cada forma reducida sale de dos o tres palabras: I would have, let me, what do you e I don't know.

prompt.es: Lee la nota del jefe. ¿Qué efecto tienen «kinda» y «lemme» en ella?

choices.text: They soften a firm request and keep the tone friendly.
They turn the request into a suggestion that anyone can ignore.
They show that the manager is unsure about the deadline.

feedback.es: El mensaje sigue pidiendo las novedades antes del mediodía; las formas informales solo suavizan el tono.

origin.text: Manager's note to the team: 'Hi all, we're kinda behind schedule, so I gotta ask everyone to send their updates by noon. Lemme know if that's a problem.'

prompt.es: Escucha a Leo y elige qué da a entender sobre la cena.

choices.text: He has already decided to cancel it, but hopes Mia will not mind.
He would like to keep it, but he cannot promise to be there.
He will be there on time, although the report is not finished yet.

feedback.es: Leo duda («I dunno if I can make it»), propone retrasar la cena y deja otra fecha como plan B: quiere mantenerla sin poder asegurarla.

origin.audio: Hey Mia, it's Leo. Listen, I'm gonna be honest: I dunno if I can make it tonight. I gotta finish the budget report, and my manager kinda expects it by nine. I'd've told you earlier, but the meeting ran over. Lemme see how far I get, and I'll text you at eight. Whaddya think, could we move dinner back an hour? If not, no worries, we'll do it another time.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué propósito menciona Leo la reunión.

choices.text: To blame his manager for the change of plan.
To ask Mia to join the meeting with him.
To explain why he did not warn Mia sooner.

feedback.es: «I'd've told you earlier, but the meeting ran over» justifica el aviso tardío: no culpa al jefe ni invita a Mia.

origin.audio: Hey Mia, it's Leo. Listen, I'm gonna be honest: I dunno if I can make it tonight. I gotta finish the budget report, and my manager kinda expects it by nine. I'd've told you earlier, but the meeting ran over. Lemme see how far I get, and I'll text you at eight. Whaddya think, could we move dinner back an hour? If not, no worries, we'll do it another time.

prompt.es: Completa con la forma reducida de «querer»: Mia invita a un amigo a cenar.

feedback.es: Wanna es want to dicho deprisa: en una pregunta informal suena Do you wanna…?

origin.text: Mia's text reads: 'We're going for pizza after the talk. Do you ___ join us, or are you too tired?'

prompt.es: Ordena la forma completa: «¿Qué quieres que le diga?»

answer.text: What do you want me to tell him

feedback.es: Whaddya wanna se escribe completo what do you want to; aquí la estructura es want + alguien + to + verbo: what do you want me to tell him.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla en el café y elige con qué fin se ofrece a ayudar la amiga.

choices.text: To let her rehearse in a realistic interview setting.
To take her place at the interview this week.
To teach her some new reduced forms before six.

feedback.es: Al hacer de entrevistador («as if I were the interviewer»), la amiga crea una práctica realista de la entrevista.

origin.audio: At the café, two friends are talking. One says she's kinda worried about her interview, so she's gonna practise out loud. The other one answers, lemme help: I'll ask the questions, and you answer as if I were the interviewer. They agree to start at six.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta adecuada para el correo del director del hospital.

choices.text: I'd've loved to start in March, but I dunno if I can confirm by Friday.
I'd be happy to start in March, and I can confirm my availability by Friday.
I'm gonna start in March, and lemme confirm the details by Friday, right?

feedback.es: Con un director se usa la forma completa y cortés; las otras respuestas mezclan formas reducidas y dudas.

origin.text: Director's email: 'Can you confirm that you will be able to start in March?'

prompt.es: Completa: estos mensajes pueden «dar la impresión de» ser fríos.

feedback.es: Come across as + adjetivo describe la impresión que causa algo o alguien, sea o no la intención.

origin.text: Messages written in capitals, with no greeting, can ___ across as cold, even when the sender is only in a hurry.

title.es: Enlaces, elisiones y acento de frase

es: Predecir cómo se enlazan y se omiten sonidos entre palabras (turn it off, next day, old man), distinguir frases casi idénticas por el acento y completar frases dictadas con la forma escrita real.

teaching.en: When people talk quickly, they blend words together, so 'pick it up' can sound like a single word with three syllables.
teaching.es: Cuando la gente habla rápido, une las palabras, de modo que «pick it up» puede sonar como una sola palabra de tres sílabas.
teaching.explanationEs: Pick it up se oye «pi-ki-tup»: las palabras se funden en un solo bloque.
segments: When people talk quickly, they blend words together, so 'pick it
up' can sound like a single word with three syllables.
teaching.audioText: When people talk quickly, they blend words together, so 'pick it up' can sound like a single word with three syllables.

teaching.en: A final consonant often links to the vowel at the start of the next word, which is why 'turn it off' sounds like 'tur-ni-toff'.
teaching.es: Una consonante final suele enlazarse con la vocal inicial de la palabra siguiente, y por eso «turn it off» suena «tur-ni-toff».
teaching.explanationEs: La n de turn y la t de it pasan a empezar la sílaba siguiente.
segments: A final consonant often links to the vowel at the start of
the next word, which is why 'turn it off' sounds like 'tur-ni-toff'.
teaching.audioText: A final consonant often links to the vowel at the start of the next word, which is why 'turn it off' sounds like 'tur-ni-toff'.

teaching.en: Many speakers drop the t in 'next day'; this elision makes two separate words run together as one smooth phrase, 'nex day'.
teaching.es: Muchos hablantes omiten la t de «next day»; esta elisión hace que dos palabras separadas se fundan en una sola frase fluida, «nex day».
teaching.explanationEs: La t casi desaparece entre dos consonantes, pero se sigue escribiendo.
segments: Many speakers drop the t in 'next day'; this elision makes
two separate words run together as one smooth phrase, 'nex day'.
teaching.audioText: Many speakers drop the t in 'next day'; this elision makes two separate words run together as one smooth phrase, 'nex day'.

teaching.en: We usually swallow the d in 'old man', so what you hear is closer to 'ol man' than to the written words.
teaching.es: Normalmente nos tragamos la d de «old man», así que lo que oyes se parece más a «ol man» que a las palabras escritas.
teaching.explanationEs: Las formas entre comillas aproximan el sonido: no son ortografía.
segments: We usually swallow the d in 'old man', so what you
hear is closer to 'ol man' than to the written words.
teaching.audioText: We usually swallow the d in 'old man', so what you hear is closer to 'ol man' than to the written words.

teaching.en: In 'We're meeting at the station', the stressed syllables are 'meet' and 'sta', while the unstressed words almost disappear.
teaching.es: En «We're meeting at the station», las sílabas acentuadas son «meet» y «sta», mientras que las palabras átonas casi desaparecen.
teaching.explanationEs: Stressed = sílaba fuerte y larga; unstressed = sílaba breve y débil.
segments: In 'We're meeting at the station', the stressed syllables are
'meet' and 'sta', while the unstressed words almost disappear.

teaching.en: Learners who cannot tell apart 'ice cream' and 'I scream' should listen for where the words link, not for the spelling.
teaching.es: Quienes no logran distinguir «ice cream» de «I scream» deberían fijarse en dónde se enlazan las palabras, no en la ortografía.
teaching.explanationEs: Las dos frases suenan casi igual; cambia dónde cae el acento y cómo se enlaza la consonante.
segments: Learners who cannot tell apart 'ice cream' and 'I scream' should
listen for where the words link, not for the spelling.

prompt.es: En «turn it off», ¿qué ocurre entre «turn» y «it» al hablar rápido?

choices.text: The n of turn disappears before the vowel of it.
The t of it is said alone after a clear pause.
The n of turn links to the vowel of it.

feedback.es: La n final de turn se enlaza con la vocal de it: no desaparece ni se separa con pausa.

hint.es: Piensa en lo que hace una consonante final ante una vocal.

origin.text: Could you turn it off before you leave? I can't concentrate with all this noise.

prompt.es: Escucha y completa: «Quedaremos al día siguiente, cuando todos hayan leído el informe.»

feedback.es: En habla rápida la t de next casi no suena («nex day»), pero la palabra se escribe completa.

hint.es: En el audio suena «nex»: escribe la palabra entera.

origin.text: We didn't finish on Friday, so we'll meet the ___ day, when everyone has had time to read the report.
origin.audio: We didn't finish on Friday, so we'll meet the next day, when everyone has had time to read the report.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Recógelo cuando tengas ocasión.»

answer.text: Pick it up when you get a chance

feedback.es: El verbo frasal pick up separa el pronombre: pick it up, y las tres palabras se enlazan al hablar.

hint.es: Empieza por el verbo frasal con el pronombre en medio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué consejo da la profesora a sus alumnos.

choices.text: Follow the rhythm of the whole phrase before analysing single words.
Write down each separate word before hearing the rhythm.
Slow the recording down until every sound is clear.

feedback.es: La profesora pide captar primero el ritmo de la frase y completar después los detalles, no analizar palabra por palabra.

origin.audio: A pronunciation coach tells her class to stop listening for separate words. In an old man, she explains, the n moves onto old and the d almost disappears, so the whole phrase sounds smooth. Her advice is to catch the rhythm first and fill in the details afterwards.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el fenómeno que ocurre al decirla rápido.

elisión: la t casi no suena
fusión: suena como una sola palabra

feedback.es: Turn it off enlaza consonante y vocal; last night y old man pierden una t o una d; kind of se funde en kinda.

prompt.es: Ana no captó la hora. ¿Qué palabras debe acentuar Mia al repetirla?

choices.text: Please, don't and late.
Meeting, station and nine.
We're, at and the.

feedback.es: Las palabras de contenido que llevan la información (meeting, station, nine) reciben el acento; las demás se debilitan.

origin.text: Mia says, quickly: 'We're meeting at the station at nine, so please don't be late.' Ana missed the time and asks her to repeat it.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué estrategia recomienda Sara.

choices.text: Write down every word on paper before thinking about the meaning.
Ask speakers to slow down until each word is separate.
Start from the stressed syllables and add the small words later.

feedback.es: Sara recomienda construir la frase a partir de las sílabas acentuadas; las palabras pequeñas encajan después.

origin.audio: In this week's language podcast, Sara explains why learners struggle with fast speech. She points out that check it out does not sound like three separate words; it sounds like one. The same happens with best friend, where the t almost disappears. Her advice is not to write down every word, but to listen for the stressed syllables and build the sentence around them. Only then, she says, do the small words fall into place.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender Sara sobre anotar cada palabra.

choices.text: That it is not the best way to follow fast speech.
That it is useful only for beginners at a slow pace.
That it is impossible even for fluent speakers.

feedback.es: Al decir «not to write down every word», Sara sugiere que no es la mejor estrategia, sin llegar a llamarla imposible.

prompt.es: Completa: la t casi muda de «best friend» es un caso de «elisión».

feedback.es: Elision es el nombre del proceso por el que un sonido se omite al hablar rápido, como la t entre dos consonantes.

origin.text: The almost silent t in best friend is an example of ___, because the sound simply disappears between two consonants.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los hablantes suelen omitir la t entre dos consonantes.»

answer.text: Speakers often drop the t between two consonants

feedback.es: Drop the t describe la elisión: el sonido casi desaparece cuando queda entre dos consonantes.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota de Tom y elige en qué se fijó al repetir la grabación.

choices.text: How fast the speaker was talking.
Which syllable carried the stress.
Whether the final s was clear.

feedback.es: Ice cream acentúa la primera sílaba; I scream acentúa scream. Ese cambio de acento le dio la pista.

origin.audio: Tom wrote I scream in his notes, but the sentence was about a dessert. When he listened again, he noticed that the stress fell on the first syllable, ice, and he realised the speaker had said ice cream.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere Ana al acentuar «she» en esta frase?

choices.text: That nobody took any money at all.
That Ana blames the person mentioned for taking it.
That someone else may have taken the money.

feedback.es: Al acentuar she, Ana niega que sea esa persona, lo que implica que otra pudo haberlo hecho.

origin.text: Ana says: 'I didn't say SHE took the money.' The stress falls on the word she.

prompt.es: Completa: al decir «first class» deprisa, la t «se omite» y las palabras se funden.

feedback.es: La t entre dos consonantes se omite en habla rápida: es un caso de elisión.

origin.text: When we say first class quickly, the t is ___ and the two words run together.

title.es: Mensajes de voz y avisos de estación

es: Extraer la idea general, las cifras, el propósito y el cambio de plan de mensajes de voz y avisos de estación dichos a velocidad natural, e inferir lo que el hablante da a entender.

teaching.en: You have one new voicemail from Ana, who says the party has moved and asks you to call her back tonight.
teaching.es: Tienes un mensaje de voz nuevo de Ana, que dice que la fiesta se ha cambiado y te pide que la llames esta noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Voicemail es el mensaje que alguien deja cuando no contestas; call back es devolver la llamada.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige por qué llama Ana.

choices.text: To announce a change and ask for a quick reply.
To invite Sara to a party for the first time.
To ask Sara to book another hall.

feedback.es: Ana avisa del cambio de día y pide una respuesta rápida: no es una invitación nueva ni una petición de sala.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que Ana pide al final, no solo en lo que cuenta.

origin.audio: Hi Sara, it's Ana. I'm just giving you a heads-up: the party has been moved to Saturday, because the hall is booked on Friday. Everyone else has said yes, so please tell me by tonight if Saturday is a problem for you. Thanks!

prompt.es: Escucha el mismo mensaje y elige hasta cuándo debe responder Sara.

choices.text: By Friday.
By tonight.
By Saturday morning.

feedback.es: El plazo aparece tras «please tell me»: esta noche. El viernes y el sábado son fechas de la sala y la fiesta.

hint.es: Busca el plazo justo después de «please tell me».

origin.audio: Hi Sara, it's Ana. I'm just giving you a heads-up: the party has been moved to Saturday, because the hall is booked on Friday. Everyone else has said yes, so please tell me by tonight if Saturday is a problem for you. Thanks!

prompt.es: Completa el aviso: «Los pasajeros a Londres deben ir ahora al andén cuatro.»

feedback.es: Platform es el andén: en las estaciones se dice platform four, con el número después.

hint.es: Es el lugar de la estación donde se sube al tren.

prompt.es: Escucha el aviso y elige qué pueden hacer los pasajeros del tren suprimido.

choices.text: Wait at the station for the same train to leave later.
Take a replacement bus to Manchester.
Take a later train or ask for their money back.

feedback.es: El aviso ofrece dos opciones: subir al siguiente tren o reclamar el reembolso; no menciona autobuses sustitutivos.

origin.audio: Attention, please. Owing to a signal failure near Crewe, all services to Manchester are subject to severe disruption. Passengers holding tickets for the cancelled service may board the next train or claim a full refund at the information desk. We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

prompt.es: Escucha el aviso otra vez y elige cuánto se retrasa el tren de las cinco y cuarto.

choices.text: About forty minutes.
About fourteen minutes.
About four minutes.

feedback.es: Forty y fourteen se confunden: forty lleva el acento al principio y fourteen al final; el aviso dice forty.

es: Producir un mensaje de voz para un amigo con bloques de sentido marcados, palabras clave acentuadas y formas reducidas, y valorar qué registro transmite cada versión.

teaching.en: A short pause after each chunk gives the listener time to take in your message, especially when it includes numbers.
teaching.es: Una pausa breve tras cada bloque da al oyente tiempo para asimilar tu mensaje, sobre todo si incluye cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada chunk es una idea completa; la pausa se marca con una barra (/).

to take in your message, especially when it includes numbers.
teaching.audioText: A short pause after each chunk gives the listener time to take in your message, especially when it includes numbers.

teaching.en: The key words, such as the time, the place and the price, carry the stress, while weak words like 'to' and 'the' are said quickly.
teaching.es: Las palabras clave, como la hora, el lugar y el precio, llevan el acento, mientras que las palabras débiles como «to» y «the» se dicen rápido.
teaching.explanationEs: Acentúa la información importante; las palabras gramaticales se debilitan.

teaching.en: If you rehearse and run through your message once aloud, you will notice where your voice starts to trail off and where a pause would sound more natural.
teaching.es: Si ensayas y repasas tu mensaje una vez en voz alta, notarás dónde se apaga tu voz y dónde una pausa sonaría más natural.
teaching.explanationEs: Rehearse = ensayar; run through = repasar de principio a fin; trail off = apagarse la voz.

teaching.en: You can emphasise a number to correct a misunderstanding, as in 'I said NINE, not five, so please don't be late.'
teaching.es: Puedes enfatizar una cifra para corregir un malentendido, como en «Dije NUEVE, no cinco, así que no llegues tarde».
teaching.explanationEs: Emphasise significa dar más fuerza a una palabra para aclarar o corregir.

teaching.en: English rhythm comes from stressed syllables arriving at roughly regular intervals, so the weak words between them get squeezed together.
teaching.es: El ritmo del inglés nace de sílabas acentuadas que llegan a intervalos más o menos regulares, así que las palabras débiles entre ellas se comprimen.
teaching.explanationEs: El ritmo depende de los acentos, no de cada sílaba.

teaching.en: A good voice note has a clear cadence: a steady pace, a pause after each chunk, and a slightly higher voice on the key information, so slow down when you reach the numbers.
teaching.es: Una buena nota de voz tiene una cadencia clara: un ritmo constante, una pausa tras cada bloque y una voz algo más aguda en la información clave, así que habla más despacio al llegar a las cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Cadence es la melodía del mensaje; slow down (hablar más despacio) ayuda si te precipitas.

feedback.es: La respuesta acepta el plan, repite hora y precio, contrapropone con razón y usa alguna forma reducida en registro informal.

origin.text: Mensajes del chat — Mia: «The concert is on Saturday at seven thirty. Who's in?» Leo: «The tickets are fifty pounds each.» Tom: «Let's meet at the station at six.» Responde en registro informal: acepta el plan, repite la hora del concierto y el precio, y contrapropón otra hora de encuentro con tu razón. Usa al menos una forma reducida.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Sara y elige qué deja entrever sobre los cambios anteriores.

choices.text: That she is happy to change everything again.
That she does not care which day they finally choose.
That she is a little impatient with the earlier changes.

feedback.es: «Please don't change your minds again» revela cierta impaciencia por los cambios anteriores.

origin.audio: Hi all, it's Sara. I'm gonna book the tickets now, so please don't change your minds again. Sunday is fine by me, but I can't meet at noon; I'd rather make it one o'clock, because my shift finishes at half past twelve. Meet me at the gate, not at the station.

prompt.es: Completa: el domingo «me viene bien», pero prefiero una hora más tarde.

feedback.es: Works for me es la fórmula informal para aceptar una propuesta, aunque luego se pida un ajuste.

origin.text: Honestly, Sunday ___ for me, but could we make it one o'clock? I finish work at half past twelve.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que rechaza la hora con naturalidad y propone otra.

choices.text: Nine's a bit late for me, honestly; could we make it half past seven?
Nine is impossible for me; I cannot accept any dinner that late.
Nine's perfect, count me in, but I'd rather skip dinner and have coffee.

feedback.es: Tom explica con suavidad por qué no le viene bien y propone otra hora; las demás opciones son tajantes o se contradicen.

origin.text: Mia asks: 'Dinner at nine on Friday?' Tom cannot stay out that late, but he wants to go.
